Wannsee Conference 1942
20 January meeting led by Heydrich coordinating 'Final Solution'; bureaucratic plan for extermination of European Jews.
Coup of Brumaire 1799
Napoleon Bonaparte's seizure of power in November 1799 that overthrew the Directory and established the Consulate, ending the revolutionary republic.
Declaration of the Rights of Man 1789
Foundational text of August 1789 proclaiming liberty, equality and popular sovereignty, dismantling the privileges of the old regime.
Estates-General 1789
Assembly of three estates summoned by Louis XVI to address France's fiscal crisis, last met in 1614, sparking the revolution when the Third Estate broke away.
Storming of the Bastille 1789
On 14 July 1789 a Paris crowd seized the royal fortress-prison, a symbol of monarchical tyranny, marking the popular outbreak of the revolution.
The Terror 1793-94
Period of mass executions directed by Robespierre's Committee of Public Safety against suspected enemies of the revolution, ending with his fall.
Thermidorian Reaction 1794
The overthrow and execution of Robespierre in July 1794, ending the Terror and ushering in the more moderate Directory regime.

Saladin's decisive victory destroying the army of the Kingdom of Jerusalem, leading directly to his recapture of Jerusalem and the Third Crusade.
Battle of Manzikert 1071
Seljuk Turks crushed the Byzantine army and captured Emperor Romanos IV, opening Anatolia to Turkish settlement and prompting later appeals to the West.
Capture of Jerusalem 1099
The First Crusade's bloody conquest of the holy city from its Muslim rulers, establishing Latin Christian control after a successful siege.
Council of Clermont 1095
Pope Urban II's sermon calling Western knights to aid Byzantium and recover Jerusalem, launching the First Crusade with the cry 'God wills it'.
Sack of Constantinople 1204
The Fourth Crusade, diverted from Egypt, captured and looted the Christian Byzantine capital, fatally weakening the empire it had set out to aid.
The Crusader States
Latin principalities founded in the East after 1099, including the Kingdom of Jerusalem and County of Edessa, collectively called Outremer.
GI Bill 1944
Servicemen's Readjustment Act provided returning veterans with college tuition, mortgages and unemployment pay; created suburban middle class.
Great Society 1964-65
Johnson's reforms: Medicare, Medicaid, Voting Rights Act, immigration reform, War on Poverty.
McCarthyism
Senator Joseph McCarthy's 1950-54 anti-communist witch hunts; HUAC investigations, Hollywood blacklist, fall of State Department officials.
Roe v Wade 1973
Supreme Court 7-2 ruling that constitutional right to privacy covered abortion; landmark of second-wave feminism.
Stonewall 1969
28 June police raid on Greenwich Village gay bar sparked riots; catalyst for gay liberation movement.
Watergate 1972-74
Nixon's cover-up of DNC headquarters break-in; impeachment proceedings forced resignation on 9 August 1974.
Big Bang 1986
Thatcher's deregulation of London Stock Exchange; abolished fixed commissions, allowed foreign ownership, transformed City.
Butskellism
Post-war consensus combining Conservative Butler and Labour Gaitskell; mixed economy, full employment, welfare state.
Falklands War 1982
Argentina invaded 2 April; British task force retook islands by 14 June; Thatcher's popularity rescued.
Suez Crisis 1956
Eden's collusion with France and Israel to seize canal from Nasser; US pressure forced humiliating withdrawal, ended Eden's career.
Three-Day Week 1974
Heath's response to NUM miners' strike and oil crisis; electricity restricted, prompted February election loss.
Winter of Discontent 1978-79
Public sector strikes under Callaghan; rubbish uncollected, dead unburied; led to Thatcher's victory May 1979.

Henry Tudor's defeat and killing of Richard III, ending the Wars of the Roses and founding the Tudor dynasty as Henry VII.

Henry VIII's closure of religious houses, seizing their wealth and land to fund the crown and reward loyal nobles and gentry.

Period of religious upheaval, rebellion and instability under Edward VI and Mary I, testing the strength of crown and government.

A royal prerogative court strengthened under the early Tudors to enforce order over overmighty subjects and bypass the slower common-law courts.
The Reformation Parliament 1529-36
Sessions of Parliament that passed Henry VIII's break with Rome, establishing royal supremacy over the Church of England.

Easter Rising 1916
24-29 April Dublin rebellion led by Pearse and Connolly; crushed by British, 15 leaders executed including Connolly tied to chair.
Government of Ireland Act 1920
Partition created Northern Ireland (six counties) and Southern Ireland; established devolved Stormont parliament.
Irish Civil War 1922-23
Pro-Treaty Free State forces under Collins defeated anti-Treaty IRA led by de Valera; Collins killed August 1922.
Republic of Ireland 1949
Declared by Costello government on Easter Monday; left Commonwealth, ended remaining ties with British Crown.
Sinn Fein 1918 Landslide
Won 73 of 105 Irish seats; refused Westminster, established Dail Eireann in Dublin January 1919.
1905 Revolution
Uprising triggered by Bloody Sunday massacre; forced Tsar Nicholas II to issue October Manifesto promising Duma.
February Revolution 1917
Strikes and mutinies in Petrograd forced Nicholas II to abdicate; Provisional Government took power.
Five-Year Plans
Stalin's industrialisation programme from 1928; rapid heavy industry growth at huge human cost in gulags.
NEP 1921
New Economic Policy under Lenin allowing small private trade and ending grain requisitioning; restored agricultural output.
October Revolution 1917
Bolshevik seizure of power in Petrograd led by Lenin and Trotsky; stormed Winter Palace, overthrew Provisional Government.
War Communism
1918-21 policy nationalising industry and forcibly requisitioning grain to win Civil War; caused mass famine.
Brown v Board 1954
Supreme Court ruling that 'separate but equal' schools were unconstitutional, overturning Plessy v Ferguson (1896).
Civil Rights Act 1964
Johnson's law banning discrimination in employment and public accommodations on grounds of race, sex, religion.
Little Rock Nine 1957
Nine black students escorted by 101st Airborne to integrate Central High School after Governor Faubus blocked them.
March on Washington 1963
250,000 gathered to hear King's 'I Have a Dream' speech; pressured Kennedy administration on civil rights bill.
Montgomery Bus Boycott 1955-56
381-day boycott sparked by Rosa Parks' arrest; led by Martin Luther King, ended bus segregation.
Voting Rights Act 1965
Banned literacy tests and provided federal oversight of registration in Southern states; doubled black voter registration.
English Civil War 1642-49
Armed conflict between Royalists supporting the king and Parliamentarians, ending in defeat for Charles I and the rise of the New Model Army.
Execution of Charles I 1649
The trial and beheading of Charles I for treason against his people, an unprecedented act establishing a republican Commonwealth.
Long Parliament 1640
Parliament summoned by Charles I to fund war with Scotland, which instead attacked royal policies, escalating tensions toward civil war.
Personal Rule 1629-40
The eleven years Charles I governed without Parliament, raising revenue by controversial means like Ship Money, deepening conflict with his subjects.
The Glorious Revolution 1688
The overthrow of James II and accession of William and Mary, leading to the Bill of Rights and a constitutional limit on royal power.
The Restoration 1660
The return of the monarchy under Charles II after the collapse of the republic, restoring king, Lords and the Church of England.

New Economic Policy 1921
Lenin's partial return to market trade and private enterprise after War Communism, aimed at reviving the shattered Soviet economy.
Nicholas II
The last Tsar of Russia, whose autocratic and incompetent rule from 1894 deepened social discontent and led to the fall of the Romanov dynasty.
October Revolution 1917
Lenin's Bolsheviks seized power from the Provisional Government in Petrograd, establishing the first communist state in Russia.
Russian Civil War 1918-21
Conflict between the Bolshevik Reds and anti-Bolshevik Whites, won by the Reds, consolidating communist control across the former empire.

the-british-experience-of-warfare-c1790-.d: The British Experience of Warfare c1790-1918
terms: Boer War 1899-1902
War in South Africa revealing weaknesses in British tactics and the poor health of recruits, spurring further army reform.
Cardwell Reforms 1868-74
Reforms abolishing the purchase of commissions and reorganising the army into county regiments, modernising Britain's military structure.
Conscription 1916
The Military Service Act introducing compulsory enlistment, ending Britain's reliance on volunteers to sustain manpower in the Great War.
Crimean War 1854-56
Conflict against Russia exposing British army failings in supply, medical care and command, prompting reforms championed by Florence Nightingale.
Haldane Reforms 1906-12
Creation of an Expeditionary Force, Territorial Army and General Staff, preparing Britain's army for a future European war.
Trench Warfare
The static, attritional fighting of the Western Front in the First World War, dominated by machine guns, artillery and barbed wire.

President Hoover's belief in limited government intervention, blamed for failing to relieve Depression suffering and his 1932 election defeat.

The severe economic slump of the 1930s bringing mass unemployment, bank failures and poverty across the United States.

Franklin Roosevelt's programme of relief, recovery and reform from 1933, using federal agencies and public works to combat the Depression.

The 1920s economic boom in the USA marked by mass production, consumer credit, rising share prices and cultural change before the crash.
Wall Street Crash 1929
The sudden collapse of US stock prices in October 1929, wiping out fortunes and triggering the worldwide Great Depression.

Elizabeth I's compromise establishing a Protestant Church of England with the monarch as Supreme Governor, seeking to unite her divided realm.
Essex Rebellion 1601
The Earl of Essex's failed revolt against Elizabeth's court, ending in his execution and exposing tensions late in her reign.
Marian Restoration 1553-58
Mary I's attempt to restore Catholicism, including the burning of Protestant heretics, earning her the later nickname 'Bloody Mary'.
Poor Law 1601
Elizabethan legislation making parishes responsible for relieving the poor, codifying earlier measures into a national system.
Spanish Armada 1588
Philip II's failed naval invasion of England, defeated by the English fleet and storms, boosting Elizabeth's prestige and Protestant confidence.
Abyssinian War 1935-36
Mussolini's successful invasion of Ethiopia, avenging Adowa and defying the League of Nations, boosting Fascist prestige at home.
Battle of Adowa 1896
Ethiopia's crushing defeat of an invading Italian army, a humiliation that ended Italy's first attempt to colonise Abyssinia.
Giolittian Era
The period of liberal reform and political management under Giovanni Giolitti before 1914, marked by industrial growth and electoral expansion.
Italy in the First World War
Italy joined the Allies in 1915 hoping for territory, but heavy losses and disappointment at the peace fed post-war discontent.
March on Rome 1922
Mussolini's Fascist demonstration that pressured King Victor Emmanuel III into appointing him Prime Minister, beginning Fascist rule.
Mussolini's Dictatorship
The consolidation of one-party Fascist control after 1925, suppressing opposition and building a totalitarian state under Il Duce.
Chinese Communist Revolution 1949
Mao Zedong's communist victory over the Nationalists, establishing the People's Republic of China and alarming the United States.
Domino Theory
The US belief that if one Asian state fell to communism its neighbours would follow, justifying intervention in Korea and Vietnam.
Korean War 1950-53
Conflict after communist North Korea invaded the South, drawing in US-led UN forces and China, ending in stalemate near the original border.
Nixon Visits China 1972
President Nixon's groundbreaking visit easing US-Chinese hostility, exploiting the Sino-Soviet split to reshape Cold War diplomacy.
Sino-Soviet Split
The growing rift between communist China and the Soviet Union from the late 1950s, dividing the communist world and reshaping Cold War alignments.
Vietnam War
The long conflict in which the USA backed South Vietnam against communist North Vietnam and the Viet Cong, ending in US withdrawal and communist victory.
